title: Jeremiah Chapter 36 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Jeremiah chapter 36 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Jeremiah Chapter 36 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Jeremiah Chapter 36.

questions.question: In which year of Jehoiakim's reign did the word from the LORD come to Jeremiah?
options: First year
Second year
Third year
Fourth year
questions.correctAnswer: Fourth year
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 36:1 states the word came to Jeremiah in the fourth year of Jehoiakim's reign.

questions.question: What was Jeremiah commanded to do with the words the LORD had spoken to him?
options: Preach them in the streets
Write them in a roll of a book
Tell only the priests
Keep them secret
questions.correctAnswer: Write them in a roll of a book
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 36:2 instructs Jeremiah to take a roll of a book and write all the words the LORD spoke to him.

questions.question: Why did the LORD hope the house of Judah would hear His words?
options: To bring them more riches
So they may return from their evil ways and be forgiven
To conquer their enemies
To build a new temple
questions.correctAnswer: So they may return from their evil ways and be forgiven
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 36:3 says the LORD hoped Judah would hear and return from evil ways so He might forgive their sin.

questions.question: Who did Jeremiah call to write down the words of the LORD?
options: Baruch the son of Neriah
Jehudi the son of Nethaniah
Gemariah the son of Shaphan
Michaiah the son of Gemariah
questions.correctAnswer: Baruch the son of Neriah
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 36:4 identifies Baruch son of Neriah as the one Jeremiah called to write the LORD's words.

questions.question: True or False: Jeremiah said he could not go into the house of the LORD because he was shut up.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 36:5 clearly states Jeremiah was shut up and could not enter the LORD's house.

questions.question: What did Jeremiah command Baruch to do with the written roll?
options: Hide it from the people
Read it in the LORD's house on the fasting day and to the people of Judah
Burn it before the king
Take it to Babylon
questions.correctAnswer: Read it in the LORD's house on the fasting day and to the people of Judah
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 36:6 instructs Baruch to read the roll in the LORD's house and to all Judah on the fasting day.

questions.question: True or False: The purpose of reading the words was so the people might present their supplication and return from evil ways.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 36:7 explains the hope that people would pray and return from evil ways after hearing the words.

questions.question: Who read the words of the LORD in the LORD's house as commanded?
options: Jeremiah
Jehudi
Baruch
Michaiah
questions.correctAnswer: Baruch
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 36:8 states Baruch did as Jeremiah commanded and read the words in the LORD's house.

questions.question: In which month and year did they proclaim a fast before the LORD?
options: Ninth month, fifth year
Fourth month, fourth year
Tenth month, third year
Sixth month, second year
questions.correctAnswer: Ninth month, fifth year
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 36:9 states the fast was proclaimed in the ninth month of the fifth year of Jehoiakim.

questions.question: Where did Baruch read the words of Jeremiah during the fast?
options: In the king's palace
In the chamber of Gemariah the son of Shaphan in the LORD's house
On the city wall
At the marketplace
questions.correctAnswer: In the chamber of Gemariah the son of Shaphan in the LORD's house
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 36:10 describes Baruch reading in the chamber of Gemariah in the LORD's house.

questions.question: Who heard the words from the book read by Baruch and then went to report to the princes?
options: Jehudi
Michaiah the son of Gemariah
Elishama the scribe
Jerahmeel the son of Hammelech
questions.correctAnswer: Michaiah the son of Gemariah
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 36:11 states Michaiah heard all the words and then reported to the princes.

questions.question: True or False: The princes asked Baruch to read the roll to them after hearing about its contents.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 36:14-15 shows the princes sent for Baruch and requested him to read the roll aloud.

questions.question: What was the reaction of the princes after hearing all the words read from the roll?
options: They rejoiced and praised God
They were afraid and decided to tell the king
They ignored the message
They immediately destroyed the roll
questions.correctAnswer: They were afraid and decided to tell the king
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 36:16 states the princes were afraid and said they would tell the king all the words.

questions.question: In what order did these events happen in Jeremiah 36: reading the roll to the people, proclaiming a fast, and Baruch writing the words?
options: Baruch writing the words, reading the roll to the people, proclaiming a fast
Proclaiming a fast, Baruch writing the words, reading the roll to the people
Baruch writing the words, proclaiming a fast, reading the roll to the people
Reading the roll to the people, Baruch writing the words, proclaiming a fast
questions.correctAnswer: Baruch writing the words, proclaiming a fast, reading the roll to the people
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 36:2-4 shows Baruch writing first; 36:9 shows the fast proclaimed later; 36:10-11 shows Baruch reading to the people last.

questions.question: True or False: Jeremiah was able to enter the house of the LORD to read the words himself.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 36:5 clearly states Jeremiah was shut up and could not enter the LORD's house, so Baruch read the words instead.

medium.title: Jeremiah Chapter 36 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Jeremiah Chapter 36 to real-life situations.

questions.question: Who was present in the scribe's chamber when Michaiah reported the words he had heard from the book?
options: Elishama, Delaiah, Elnathan, Gemariah, Zedekiah, and other princes
Jeremiah, Baruch, Jehoiakim, and his servants
Josiah, Jehoiakim, and the priests
Michaiah alone
questions.correctAnswer: Elishama, Delaiah, Elnathan, Gemariah, Zedekiah, and other princes
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 36:12 specifies that Michaiah went into the king's house to the scribe's chamber, where all the princes were present: Elishama, Delaiah, Elnathan, Gemariah, Zedekiah, and all the princes.

questions.question: What did Michaiah do after hearing the words of the LORD read by Baruch?
options: He declared all the words he had heard to the princes
He immediately told the king
He destroyed the scroll
He wrote a new scroll himself
questions.correctAnswer: He declared all the words he had heard to the princes
questions.explanation: According to Jeremiah 36:13, Michaiah declared all the words he heard from the book to the princes, sharing the message Baruch had read.

questions.question: What instructions did the princes send to Baruch after hearing the words from the roll?
options: To bring the roll to them and read it again
To burn the roll immediately
To hide the roll and not show it to anyone
To rewrite the roll in a more concise form
questions.correctAnswer: To bring the roll to them and read it again
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 36:14 describes how the princes sent Jehudi to bring Baruch and the roll to them so that Baruch could read it again in their ears.

questions.question: How did the princes react after hearing all the words from the roll read by Baruch?
options: They were afraid and decided to report the words to the king
They rejoiced and praised the LORD
They ignored the words and dismissed Baruch
They immediately burned the roll
questions.correctAnswer: They were afraid and decided to report the words to the king
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 36:16 states that upon hearing the words, the princes were afraid and said they would surely tell the king all these words.

questions.question: What was Baruch's explanation about how he wrote the words in the book?
options: Jeremiah spoke the words aloud and Baruch wrote them with ink
Baruch received the words in a dream and wrote them
The words were dictated by the king
Baruch wrote down words he heard from the people
questions.correctAnswer: Jeremiah spoke the words aloud and Baruch wrote them with ink
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 36:18 records Baruch's answer that Jeremiah pronounced all the words to him with his mouth, and Baruch wrote them with ink in the book.

questions.question: What advice did the princes give to Baruch and Jeremiah after hearing the words?
options: Go hide and let no man know where you are
Present the roll directly to the king
Destroy the roll to avoid trouble
Read the roll publicly again immediately
questions.correctAnswer: Go hide and let no man know where you are
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 36:19 shows that the princes urged Baruch to hide himself along with Jeremiah so that no one would know their whereabouts, likely for their protection.

questions.question: Where was the roll kept after the princes went to the king's court?
options: In the chamber of Elishama the scribe
With the king in the throne room
Buried outside the city
With Baruch and Jeremiah
questions.correctAnswer: In the chamber of Elishama the scribe
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 36:20 states the roll was laid up in the chamber of Elishama the scribe when the princes went to the king's court.

questions.question: Who did the king send to fetch the roll from Elishama's chamber?
options: Jehudi
Baruch
Michaiah
Jeremiah
questions.correctAnswer: Jehudi
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 36:21 tells that the king sent Jehudi to fetch the roll from Elishama's chamber, and Jehudi read it in the ears of the king and his princes.

questions.question: What was the setting where the king sat while Jehudi read the roll to him?
options: In the winterhouse with a fire burning on the hearth
In the temple courtyard with priests
In the palace garden during the day
In the throne room surrounded by soldiers
questions.correctAnswer: In the winterhouse with a fire burning on the hearth
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 36:22 describes the king sitting in the winterhouse in the ninth month with a fire burning before him while Jehudi read the roll.

questions.question: What did Jehudi do after reading three or four leaves of the roll to the king?
options: He cut it with a penknife and cast it into the fire
He stopped reading and returned the roll
He rewrote the message in a shorter form
He delivered the message to the princes
questions.correctAnswer: He cut it with a penknife and cast it into the fire
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 36:23 recounts Jehudi cutting the roll with a penknife after reading three or four leaves and casting it into the fire on the hearth.

questions.question: How did the king and his servants react after hearing the words from the roll?
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 36:24 indicates that neither the king nor his servants were afraid or rent their garments after hearing the words, showing a lack of fear or repentance.

questions.question: Did Elnathan, Delaiah, and Gemariah successfully persuade the king to not burn the roll?
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 36:25 states that although Elnathan, Delaiah, and Gemariah interceded to the king not to burn the roll, he refused to listen to them.

questions.question: What did the LORD do when the king commanded to take Baruch and Jeremiah into custody?
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 36:26 says the LORD hid Baruch and Jeremiah when the king commanded men to seize them, demonstrating divine protection.

questions.question: According to Jeremiah 36:28-29, what was Jeremiah instructed to do after the king burned the first roll?
options: Write another roll with all the former words and tell the king the consequences
Stop writing and remain silent
Write a shorter message to please the king
Go into hiding and cease prophesying
questions.correctAnswer: Write another roll with all the former words and tell the king the consequences
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 36:28-29 commands Jeremiah to write another roll containing all the words from the burned roll and to declare to Jehoiakim the consequences of burning it.

questions.question: How does Jeremiah 36:16-19 teach us about the importance of obedience and courage when sharing God's word?
options: Even when fearful, sharing the truth is necessary, and God’s servants may need protection
It is better to hide the message to avoid conflict
Only the king should hear God’s words
Fear should prevent sharing difficult messages
questions.correctAnswer: Even when fearful, sharing the truth is necessary, and God’s servants may need protection
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 36:16-19 shows the princes' fear but also their commitment to report the words to the king, instructing Jeremiah and Baruch to hide for safety, teaching that obedience to God’s message requires courage and sometimes protection.

hard.title: Jeremiah Chapter 36 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Jeremiah Chapter 36.

questions.question: What did Jehudi do with the scroll after reading three or four leaves to King Jehoiakim?
options: He returned it to Baruch
He hid it in the king's chamber
He cut it with a penknife and cast it into the fire
He gave it to the princes
questions.correctAnswer: He cut it with a penknife and cast it into the fire
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 36:23 states that Jehudi cut the scroll with a penknife and cast it into the fire on the hearth until the whole roll was consumed.

questions.question: How did King Jehoiakim and his servants react when they heard all the words of the scroll?
options: They rent their garments in mourning
They were afraid and repented
They were not afraid nor rent their garments
They immediately obeyed the prophet
questions.correctAnswer: They were not afraid nor rent their garments
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 36:24 reports that neither the king nor his servants showed fear or tore their garments after hearing the words.

questions.question: Who interceded with King Jehoiakim to prevent him from burning the scroll?
options: Jeremiah, Baruch, and Jehudi
Elnathan, Delaiah, and Gemariah
Michaiah, Elishama, and Zedekiah
Jerahmeel, Seraiah, and Shelemiah
questions.correctAnswer: Elnathan, Delaiah, and Gemariah
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 36:25 states that these three princes made intercession to the king to spare the scroll, but he refused to listen.

questions.question: What did King Jehoiakim command after burning the scroll regarding Jeremiah and Baruch?
options: To reward them for their prophecy
To imprison them in the dungeon
To take them into custody
To send them into exile
questions.correctAnswer: To take them into custody
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 36:26 says the king commanded certain men to take Baruch and Jeremiah, but the LORD hid them.

questions.question: What did the LORD command Jeremiah to do after the king burned the original scroll?
options: To stop prophesying
To write a new scroll with all the former words and more
To flee to Egypt
To confront the king publicly
questions.correctAnswer: To write a new scroll with all the former words and more
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 36:28 instructs Jeremiah to take another scroll and write again all the words that were in the first scroll, plus many like words.

questions.question: According to the LORD, what would happen to Jehoiakim as punishment for burning the scroll?
options: He would reign longer than his father
He would have no one to sit on the throne of David
He would be exiled to Babylon
He would be killed by his servants
questions.correctAnswer: He would have no one to sit on the throne of David
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 36:30 declares that Jehoiakim will have no descendants to sit on David's throne and his dead body would be exposed to heat and frost.

questions.question: What is the significance of the LORD saying Jehoiakim’s body would be exposed to heat by day and frost by night?
options: It foreshadows a dishonorable burial
It symbolizes his rise to power
It indicates a peaceful death at home
It shows his body will be taken to Egypt
questions.correctAnswer: It foreshadows a dishonorable burial
questions.explanation: The exposure to heat and frost in Jeremiah 36:30 implies a dishonorable death and burial, common for those rejected by God.

questions.question: What literary device is prominently used in Jeremiah 36:28-32 when describing the rewriting of the scroll?
options: Chiasm
Inclusio
Typology
Parallelism
questions.correctAnswer: Inclusio
questions.explanation: The passage forms an inclusio by beginning and ending with the theme of rewriting the scroll, emphasizing continuity despite opposition (Jeremiah 36:28, 36:32).

questions.question: What does the Hebrew word for 'roll' (megillah) in Jeremiah 36 signify in the ancient Near Eastern context?
options: A small tablet used for laws
A ceremonial cloth
A scroll used for official records or sacred text
A musical instrument
questions.correctAnswer: A scroll used for official records or sacred text
questions.explanation: The Hebrew term 'megillah' refers to a scroll, commonly used for official or sacred writings as in Jeremiah 36:2 where Jeremiah is commanded to write on the roll.

questions.question: Which other Bible passage echoes the theme of a prophet’s scroll being destroyed due to its message and then rewritten?
options: Ezekiel 2:9-10
Isaiah 6:1-10
Daniel 5:1-31
Malachi 3:1-5
questions.correctAnswer: Ezekiel 2:9-10
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 2:9-10 describes a scroll with lamentations and woes given to Ezekiel, similar to Jeremiah 36 where a scroll contains prophetic judgment and must be preserved despite opposition.

questions.question: How does Jeremiah 36:29-31 fulfill the theme found in 2 Kings 24:6-7 about Jehoiakim’s reign?
options: It predicts Jehoiakim’s peaceful reign
It confirms Jehoiakim’s rebellion and downfall
It praises Jehoiakim’s military victories
It describes Jehoiakim’s exile to Egypt
questions.correctAnswer: It confirms Jehoiakim’s rebellion and downfall
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 36:29-31 prophesies Jehoiakim’s judgment for rebellion, consistent with 2 Kings 24:6-7 which recounts his evil deeds and demise.

questions.question: What theme from Jeremiah 36 connects to Jesus' role as the ultimate prophet who speaks God's word despite rejection, as seen in which New Testament passage?
options: Matthew 23:37
John 1:1-14
Romans 8:28
questions.explanation: Acts 3:22-23 quotes Moses saying God will raise a prophet like him, underscoring Jesus’ fulfillment of the prophetic role despite rejection, paralleling Jeremiah's experience in chapter 36.

questions.question: True or False: Baruch wrote the words of the LORD from Jeremiah’s mouth on a scroll as commanded by Jeremiah.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 36:4 shows Baruch writing all the words of the LORD as Jeremiah dictated.

questions.question: True or False: After King Jehoiakim burned the scroll, he immediately repented and sought the LORD's forgiveness.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 36:31 explains that the people, including Jehoiakim, did not heed the warnings and judgment pronounced against them.

questions.question: What was the purpose of Jeremiah commanding Baruch to read the scroll aloud on the fasting day in the LORD's house?
options: To entertain the people
To encourage the people to repent and pray
To confuse the priests
To announce a new king
questions.correctAnswer: To encourage the people to repent and pray
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 36:3-7 indicates the reading was to warn Judah so they might turn from evil and seek forgiveness from the LORD.

theological.title: Jeremiah Chapter 36 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Jeremiah Chapter 36 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What was the primary purpose God gave Jeremiah for writing down the words spoken against Israel, Judah, and the nations?
options: To bring judgment without hope for repentance
To ensure the king’s approval
So that the house of Judah might hear and return from their evil ways
To prepare the people for exile without warning
questions.correctAnswer: So that the house of Judah might hear and return from their evil ways
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 36:3 states that the purpose was so the house of Judah might hear the evil God purposed to do, return from their evil ways, and receive forgiveness.

questions.question: Which doctrinal truth about divine revelation is illustrated by Jeremiah commanding Baruch to write down God's words as spoken to him?
options: The infallibility of the written word as dictated by God
The necessity of public oral tradition only
The rejection of written scripture in favor of prophecy
The autonomy of human wisdom over divine words
questions.correctAnswer: The infallibility of the written word as dictated by God
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 36:4 shows Baruch writing exactly what Jeremiah dictated from God's mouth, demonstrating the reliability and divine origin of the written prophetic word, a foundation for Scripture's authority.

questions.question: What attribute of God is revealed by His command to rewrite the scroll after King Jehoiakim burned the first one?
options: Omnipotence in controlling human actions
Immutability in His word despite human rejection
Impatience toward sinners
Partiality toward kings
questions.correctAnswer: Immutability in His word despite human rejection
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 36:27-28 shows God's unchanging commitment to His message despite Jehoiakim's destructive act, illustrating the immutability of divine truth.

questions.question: How does Jeremiah 36 demonstrate the doctrine of human sinfulness and rebellion against God?
options: By showing the king's obedience to God's commands
Through the burning of God's word and ignoring warnings
By the people's immediate repentance
Because the princes praised Jeremiah's message
questions.correctAnswer: Through the burning of God's word and ignoring warnings
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 36:23-25 highlights the king burning the scroll and refusing to listen to intercessions, depicting blatant rebellion and hardness of heart against God's revelation.

questions.question: What theological insight is gained by combining Jeremiah 36:6 and Jeremiah 36:11 regarding the reading of the scroll to the people?
options: God's word is meant only for private meditation
Public proclamation of God's word aims to provoke repentance
Prophets should only speak to kings
The people were eager to hear God's judgment
questions.correctAnswer: Public proclamation of God's word aims to provoke repentance
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 36:6 commands reading the scroll publicly to all Judah, and Jeremiah 36:11 describes the people's hearing, emphasizing the role of public proclamation in calling for repentance.

questions.question: Which attribute of God is most clearly demonstrated when He hides Jeremiah and Baruch from the king’s officers sent to arrest them?
options: Divine omniscience
Divine providence and protection
Divine wrath
Divine silence
questions.correctAnswer: Divine providence and protection
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 36:26 shows God actively hiding Jeremiah and Baruch from harm, reflecting His providential care for His servants amidst persecution.

questions.question: How does Jeremiah 36:30-31 contribute to the doctrine of divine judgment on rulers and their descendants?
options: It promises eternal reign for Jehoiakim's dynasty
It pronounces an end to Jehoiakim's throne and punishment for his seed
It grants Jehoiakim a chance for repentance and forgiveness
It ignores the king's sins and focuses on the people
questions.correctAnswer: It pronounces an end to Jehoiakim's throne and punishment for his seed
questions.explanation: Verses 30-31 declare that Jehoiakim will have no successor on David’s throne and that both he and his descendants will face punishment for their iniquity, highlighting God's sovereign judgment over kings.

questions.question: What narrative arc connecting Jeremiah 36 to the broader story of redemption is illustrated by the prophecy against Jehoiakim's reign?
options: The failure of David’s royal line and the need for a Messiah
The eternal success of all Davidic kings
Immediate restoration of Israel without exile
The abolishment of prophecy in Israel
questions.correctAnswer: The failure of David’s royal line and the need for a Messiah
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 36:30-31 reveals the judgment against Jehoiakim’s line, pointing forward to the break in the Davidic monarchy and the eventual Messianic hope for restoration, fitting within redemptive history.

questions.question: What does the reaction of the princes after hearing the scroll (Jeremiah 36:16) reveal about human response to divine truth?
options: Immediate acceptance and joy
Fear and intention to report to the king without repentance
Rebellion and mocking of the word
Complete indifference
questions.correctAnswer: Fear and intention to report to the king without repentance
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 36:16 states the princes were afraid and planned to tell the king, showing a fearful but non-repentant response to God's word.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that divine prophecy is unreliable since a king could simply destroy written words. What does Jeremiah 36:27-29 teach about the durability of God's word despite human opposition?
options: God’s word can be lost if destroyed physically
God commands the rewriting of the scroll, confirming His word’s perseverance
The prophecy ends with the burning of the scroll
Human actions can nullify divine prophecy
questions.correctAnswer: God commands the rewriting of the scroll, confirming His word’s perseverance
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 36:27-29 shows God directing Jeremiah to write another scroll with the same words after the king burned the first, demonstrating that divine prophecy endures beyond human attempts to suppress it.

questions.question: What theological doctrine is illustrated by the king’s refusal to repent even after hearing God’s judgment through Jeremiah’s scroll?
options: The doctrine of election
The doctrine of divine sovereignty over human will
The doctrine of human stubbornness and rejection of grace
The doctrine of universal salvation
questions.correctAnswer: The doctrine of human stubbornness and rejection of grace
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 36:24-25 reveal the king and his servants were not afraid nor did they repent, illustrating humanity’s capacity to resist God’s call to repentance.

questions.question: Combining Jeremiah 36:2 and Jeremiah 36:32, what does the process of writing and rewriting the scroll signify about the transmission of Scripture?
options: Scripture was preserved through divine inspiration despite human attempts to destroy it
Writing was unreliable and frequently inaccurate
Only oral tradition mattered for God’s word
The first scroll was complete and needed no additions
questions.correctAnswer: Scripture was preserved through divine inspiration despite human attempts to destroy it
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 36:2 commands writing all God’s words, and 36:32 shows the second scroll included the first’s words plus additional ones, indicating divine preservation and ongoing revelation.

questions.question: What does the instruction in Jeremiah 36:6 about reading the scroll on a fasting day reveal about the role of corporate repentance in God’s plan?
options: Corporate fasting and hearing God’s word are means to prompt national repentance
Fasting was merely a ritual without significance
The scroll was only for private reading
Fasting was to be done without hearing prophetic words
questions.correctAnswer: Corporate fasting and hearing God’s word are means to prompt national repentance
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 36:6 links reading God’s word publicly on a fasting day with the hope that people will repent, highlighting the role of corporate spiritual discipline in sanctification.

questions.question: How does the narrative in Jeremiah 36:10-13 illustrate the social dynamics of prophetic ministry within a corrupt society?
options: Prophecy was universally accepted and honored
Prophetic messages were heard but quickly taken to authorities who often opposed them
Prophets only spoke to kings in private
Prophecy was ignored by all social classes
questions.correctAnswer: Prophetic messages were heard but quickly taken to authorities who often opposed them
questions.explanation: Verses 10-13 show Baruch reading publicly, Michaiah hearing and reporting the words to princes, indicating that prophetic warnings circulated but were met with opposition by ruling elites.

questions.question: What combined doctrinal teaching emerges from Jeremiah 36:19 and Jeremiah 36:26 about God's protection of His servants and the reality of persecution?
options: God abandons His servants during trials
God provides hidden protection even amid hostile opposition
Persecution is always a sign of divine rejection
Servants of God are never endangered
questions.correctAnswer: God provides hidden protection even amid hostile opposition
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 36:19 advises hiding Jeremiah and Baruch, and 36:26 reports God hid them from arrest, teaching that divine protection accompanies faithful service despite persecution.
